G7932093.description: Ngwenya is a town in western Eswatini, lying near the border with South Africa, north west of Mbabane, on the MR3 road. The South African town opposite Ngwenya is Oshoek in Mpumalanga province.

G934840.description: Tshaneni is a town in northern Eswatini (Swaziland), near the border post on the South African border. There are extensive sugar plantations around Tshaneni, and it is near the Sand River reservoir.

G934851.description: Siteki is a town in eastern Eswatini, lying west of the Lebombo Mountains, with an estimated population of 6,381 as of 2013. It is named for a declaration of Mbandzeni permitting his troops to marry.

G934862.description: Sidvokodvo is a town in central Eswatini, situated south of Manzini. It used to host Eswatini Railway's steam shed, but steam traction has long been abandoned in Eswatini.

G934881.description: Piggs Peak is a town in northwestern Eswatini. It was founded around gold prospecting in 1884, but its main industry is now forestry.

G934900.description: Nsoko is a town in southern Eswatini located in the Lubombo region about five kilometres (3.1 mi) from the border with South Africa. It lies about 65 kilometres (40 mi) north-east of Lavumisa and 45 kilometres (28 mi) south-east of Maloma.

G934913.description: Nhlangano (Swazi: [n̩ɬáŋanɔ]) is the fourth largest town in Eswatini. It is the capital of the southern district of Shiselweni.

G934966.description: This is a list of cities and towns in Eswatini. The table below also includes the population and region information.

G934971.description: Mhlambanyatsi is a town in western Eswatini. It is located 18 kilometres southwest of the capital, Mbabane.

G934985.description: Mbabane () is the most populous city in Eswatini (previously called Swaziland), and is one of the two capitals (along with Lobamba), serving as the executive capital. It has an estimated population of 94,874 (2010).

G934995.description: Manzini (formerly Bremersdorp) is a large city in Eswatini, which is also the city of Eswatini's Manzini Region. The city is the country's second largest urban center behind the capital Mbabane, with a population of 110,000 (2008).

G935005.description: Malkerns is a town in Eswatini, located in the Manzini District, between Ezulwini and Manzini. The town was inaugurated in 2012.

G935048.description: Lobamba is a town in Eswatini located in between Eswatini's two main cities, Mbabane and Manzini. It is located in the Hhohho region, with Mbabane as the nearest city and Lusushwana river as the nearest river.

G935051.description: Lavumisa is a town located in the Shiselweni district of southern Eswatini. It was named after Queen LaVumisa Ndwandwe, a wife of King Sobhuza I.

G935055.description: Kubuta is an inkhundla of Eswatini, located in the Shiselweni District. Its population as of the 2007 census was 6,922.

G935076.description: Hluti is a town situated in the Shiselweni region of Eswatini, located beyond Nhlangano and before Lavumisa As of 2005, it has a population of 6,763. It is made up of two constituencies; Shiselweni I and Hosea inkundla.

G935081.description: Hlatikulu is a town located in the Shiselweni district of southern Eswatini.

G935111.description: Bulembu is a small town located in northwestern Hhohho, Eswatini, 10 km west of the town of Piggs Peak and close to the border with South Africa. Located above the Komati Valley in Eswatini's Highveld, Bulembu is named after the siSwati word for a spider's web.
